description: Beat the Heat in Houston is a web tool or resource listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by National Center for Atmospheric Research. This map displays places in Houston where people can go to get or stay cool, such as libraries, pools, and community centers. It also displays a layer showing a model simulation of the average summer high temperatures. Click any icon on the map to get more information about the public place. Coverage: the United States, or as stated on the tool page. The toolkit lists hazards: Extreme Heat. Assets: People. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the tool itself was not opened or run, its licence and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support climate-adaptation planning and exposure screening. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.
